prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1142; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot. The insured's vehicle was struck while stationary, and the driver of the other vehicle has been identified through the reporting party. The insured driver is named on the policy and coverage is confirmed as in force on the date of loss.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. It places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact and records the position of both cars, which matches the account given at first contact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 3: Photographs submitted by the insured show the damage area and the lot layout. They confirm some of the reported details, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the impact.

Entry 4: The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office. The claimant has reported a concussion, and the kind and force of the impact appear consistent with that injury. No earlier injury to the same body area is known.

Entry 5: Medical records received. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. The treating physician's notes are consistent with the timeline described in earlier statements.

Entry 6: Review of the vehicle damage estimate raises a question about whether all listed repairs stem from this impact. Further assessment has been requested before that portion is accepted. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage period.

Entry 7: The claimant has given the same account in every conversation to date, with no material differences in sequence or description. File remains open pending the requested damage assessment and final medical review.
